name: StreamingLLM
title: Efficient Streaming Language Models with Attention Sinks
mechanism: Keep KV of the first few tokens (attention sinks, default 4) plus a rolling window of recent tokens; position-based FIFO eviction of the middle; positions re-assigned inside the cache.
evaluated_benchmarks: PG19 concatenated test set (100 books) streaming language-modeling perplexity, up to 4M tokens
Streaming QA: ARC-Challenge + ARC-Easy Q/A pairs concatenated into one stream (exact match per answer)
StreamEval (authors' benchmark inspired by LongEval line retrieval; query every 10 lines)
LongBench subset (appendix): NarrativeQA, Qasper, HotpotQA, 2WikiMQA, GovReport, MultiNews vs truncation baseline
Ablations (number of sink tokens, cache size) on PG19 perplexity
MT-Bench questions used only in the streaming chatbot demo (not a scored eval) [repo]
budgets: Cache 2048 (Llama-2) / 1024 (Falcon, Pythia, MPT) for PPL; 4 sinks + 1020 recent in the Llama-2-13B PG19 example; LongBench appendix 4+3496 and 1750+1750.
task_sensitivity_findings: Window-only attention collapses once initial tokens are evicted (Llama-2-13B PG19 first book: PPL 5158 window vs 5.40 with 4 sinks). Stable on streaming QA/dialogue that depends on recent context. Does not extend context or give long-term memory; authors say it is unsuitable for long-document QA/summarization (a book summary would cover only the last paragraphs). On LongBench, 4+3496 underperforms truncation because the initial instruction is lost; 1750+1750 only matches truncation.

name: H2O
title: H2O: Heavy-Hitter Oracle for Efficient Generative Inference of Large Language Models
mechanism: Keep heavy hitters (tokens with the largest accumulated attention scores) plus a recent window; greedy eviction framed as dynamic submodular maximization.
evaluated_benchmarks: lm-eval-harness: COPA, MathQA, OpenBookQA, PiQA, RTE, Winogrande (few-shot, e.g. 5-shot OpenBookQA)
HELM summarization: XSUM, CNN/DailyMail (1000 test samples)
Throughput benchmarks vs DeepSpeed ZeRO-Inference, HF Accelerate, FlexGen (OPT-6.7B/30B)
budgets: KV budget as % of prompt length: 4%, 10%, 20%, 60% [likely]; default 20% = 10% heavy + 10% recent [verified].
task_sensitivity_findings: Heavy hitters correlate with frequent co-occurrence; removing them causes significant degradation. Recent-only ('Local') and static-sparsity baselines degrade sharply at low budgets (a secondary summary says up to ~37%) [likely]; H2O stays near full-cache at 20%. Every workload is short-context (<2K) MC or short summarization; there is no long-context retrieval or multi-turn workload.

name: Scissorhands
title: Scissorhands: Exploiting the Persistence of Importance Hypothesis for LLM KV Cache Compression at Test Time
mechanism: Persistence of importance: tokens pivotal (high attention) earlier stay pivotal; keep a fixed-budget cache and drop tokens that were repeatedly low-attention within a history window, protecting recent tokens.
evaluated_benchmarks: Few-shot downstream: HellaSwag, MathQA, PIQA, Winogrande
models: OPT-6.7B, OPT-13B, OPT-30B, OPT-66B [likely; largest tested is OPT-66B]
budgets: 2x to 5x KV compression; up to 20x with 4-bit quantization.
task_sensitivity_findings: Up to 5x KV reduction without accuracy loss; OPT-66B keeps Winogrande/MathQA accuracy at 5x. Perplexity tolerates less compression than few-shot accuracy (maintained only to roughly 50-75% of cache depending on size; wording ambiguous) [likely]. Accuracy-vs-compression is flatter for larger models. Heavy hitters vary more in higher layers, so later layers need more budget (per cold-compress README) [likely].

name: FastGen
title: Model Tells You What to Discard: Adaptive KV Cache Compression for LLMs
repo: https://github.com/machilusZ/FastGen (no code; points to AnswerDotAI/cold-compress reimplementation and microsoft/MInference)
mechanism: Profile each head's attention on the prompt at the end of prefill, then give each head a hybrid policy (special tokens, punctuation, locality window, frequency/heavy-hitter, or full cache) chosen to recover a target fraction of attention mass.
evaluated_benchmarks: AlpacaEval (805 prompts; instruction-finetuned Llama 1; win rate vs full-cache model)
TQA (described as reading comprehension; likely TriviaQA)
budgets: KV cache budget swept 30%-100%.
task_sensitivity_findings: Compressibility grows with model size: at a 45% win rate FastGen prunes 44.9% of the cache on Llama-1-65B vs 16.9% on 7B; memory reduction at >45% win rate is ~40% (65B), ~30% (30B), ~20% (13B/7B). On 30B, FastGen at 50% compression beats fixed policies at 15%. Special-token 'anchor' heads must keep those tokens [likely]. No long-context workloads.

name: TOVA
title: Transformers are Multi-State RNNs
mechanism: Token Omission Via Attention: when the fixed-size multi-state (KV cache) is full, drop the token with the lowest attention from the current query (averaged over heads); training-free.
evaluated_benchmarks: Long story generation (full-model stories average 1566 tokens; judging protocol unverified)
budgets: Multi-state sizes as fractions of context from 1/8 to full (exact grid e.g. 64-4096 unverified).
task_sensitivity_findings: LM within 0.4 PPL of topline at 1/8 of context. SQuALITY within 1 ROUGE at 1/4 (Mistral, Yi) or 1/8 (LLaMA-2). QASPER (QA) is most sensitive and needs about 1/2 of the cache. Up to 4.8x throughput. Retained tokens: first token, punctuation, possessive endings, proper nouns.

name: Keyformer
title: Keyformer: KV Cache Reduction through Key Tokens Selection for Efficient Generative Inference
mechanism: Keep a recent window w plus k-w key tokens scored by a Gumbel-noise-regularized softmax of the logits with a temperature schedule (accumulated, biased toward initial tokens); constant-size cache k.
evaluated_benchmarks: XSUM (download script in repo; paper use unverified)
lm-eval-harness few-shot: PIQA, Winogrande, OpenBookQA, COPA [likely]
budgets: KV cache as % of prompt length, swept (repo default kv_cache 60% with recent 30%); 50% for long summarization.
task_sensitivity_findings: Reaches baseline accuracy with 70% of prompt KV for summarization but needs 90% for conversation (SODA), so dialogue is more sensitive; window attention and H2O never reach baseline. Long-document summarization (GovReport 8K) reaches baseline at 50%, with 2.1x latency and 2.4x throughput gains.

name: SnapKV
title: SnapKV: LLM Knows What You are Looking for Before Generation
mechanism: An observation window of the last prompt tokens (32) votes via attention for important prefix positions per head; votes are pooled (kernel 7, max-pool) to keep clusters; one-shot compression of the prompt KV.
evaluated_benchmarks: LongBench (16 English datasets: NarrativeQA, Qasper, MultiFieldQA-en, HotpotQA, 2WikiMQA, MuSiQue, GovReport, QMSum, MultiNews, TREC, TriviaQA, SAMSum, PassageCount, PassageRetrieval-en, LCC, RepoBench-P)
Needle-in-a-Haystack with LWM-Text-Chat-1M up to 380K tokens
Command-R case study: NIAH, RAG citation generation, lost-in-the-middle style position analysis
Observation analyses on UltraChat (multi-turn) and QMSum
budgets: Prompt KV compressed to 1024 / 2048 / 4096 tokens (window 32, pooling kernel 7).
task_sensitivity_findings: About 92% compression (1024 tokens) with performance comparable to full KV averaged over the 16 LongBench datasets. NIAH holds to 380K on one A100-80GB. Command-R keeps ~98.8% of RAG-citation performance. Assumes the question is in the observation window; the query-after-compression / multi-turn case is untested [inference].

name: PyramidKV
title: PyramidKV: Dynamic KV Cache Compression based on Pyramidal Information Funneling
venue: arXiv (OpenReview submission exists; peer-reviewed venue unknown)
mechanism: SnapKV-style observation-window token selection with a pyramidal per-layer budget: more KV in lower layers (scattered attention), less in higher layers (focused attention).
evaluated_benchmarks: LongBench (16 English datasets: NarrativeQA, Qasper, MultiFieldQA-en, HotpotQA, 2WikiMQA, MuSiQue, GovReport, QMSum, MultiNews, TREC, TriviaQA, SAMSum, PassageCount, PassageRetrieval-en, LCC, RepoBench-P) (paper text says 17 datasets)
budgets: Main results at KV sizes 128 and 2048 (range 64-2048 in sweeps); NIAH example 96; 128 entries for LLaMA-3-70B NIAH.
task_sensitivity_findings: Gains over uniform budgets are largest at small budgets (KV=128). At 0.7% retention, up to +20.5 absolute accuracy on TREC (few-shot ICL), implying uniform tiny budgets collapse on in-context-example tasks. Matches full KV with 12% retained. LLaMA-3-70B reaches 100% NIAH with 128 entries.

name: PyramidInfer
title: PyramidInfer: Pyramid KV Cache Compression for High-throughput LLM Inference
mechanism: Layer-wise decaying retention of pivotal contexts (PvCs) chosen by attention from the most recent tokens (distance-weighted); computes fewer KV in deeper layers during prefill; compresses extra generated tokens past a threshold during generation (prompt KV not re-compressed).
budgets: Over 54% GPU-memory reduction in KV cache; throughput 2.2x vs Accelerate, 1.4x vs DeepSpeed, 2.4x vs H2O.
task_sensitivity_findings: Per-task sensitivity statements not recovered (unknown). Only 2023-24 method here to cover MMLU/BBH/GSM8K/HumanEval/MT-Bench/LEval together.

name: NACL
title: NACL: A General and Effective KV Cache Eviction Framework for LLMs at Inference Time
mechanism: One-shot, layer-progressive, head-wise eviction at encoding time: Proxy-Tokens Eviction (attention from task-specific proxy tokens such as the question) combined with Random Eviction (head-wise sampling from the score distribution) to counter attention bias.
evaluated_benchmarks: Paper: short-text and long-text task suites (exact lists unknown; LongBench likely)
Repo (post-paper): InfiniteBench-128K, 12 tasks: En.Sum, En.QA, En.MC, En.Dia, Zh.QA, Code.Debug, Code.Run, Math.Calc, Math.Find, Retrieve.PassKey, Retrieve.Number, Retrieve.KV
budgets: Up to 5x KV reduction (paper); repo InfiniteBench run at 80% eviction (20% kept).
task_sensitivity_findings: Paper: +80% short-text and +76% long-text over prior eviction, >95% performance at up to 5x reduction; criticizes prior perplexity-on-short-text evaluation. Repo InfiniteBench at 80% eviction (full -> NACL): PassKey 1.000->1.000, Number 0.995->0.966, Retrieve.KV 0.592->0.036 (collapse), En.Sum 0.276->0.265, En.MC 0.664->0.664, En.Dia 0.170->0.155. Authors call Retrieve.KV one of the hardest tasks for eviction at ~20% budgets.

name: L2-norm (Devoto et al.)
title: A Simple and Effective L2 Norm-Based Strategy for KV Cache Compression
mechanism: Keep tokens whose key embeddings have the lowest L2 norm (low key norm correlates with high attention); needs no attention scores, so FlashAttention-compatible; first layers can be skipped.
budgets: keep_ratio swept 0.1-0.9; skip layers 0,1 (and 12 in NIAH/passkey runs).
task_sensitivity_findings: Lossless at 50% compression on language modeling and NIAH but at 90% on passkey retrieval, so natural-text NIAH is more sensitive than synthetic passkey.

name: SirLLM
title: SirLLM: Streaming Infinite Retentive LLM
mechanism: StreamingLLM cache (4 sinks) plus retention of high token-entropy key tokens with a memory-decay factor that gradually forgets older retained tokens.
evaluated_benchmarks: Grocery Shopping (constructed; recall items mentioned earlier)
Rock-Paper-Scissors (constructed; track user preferences over many rounds)
budgets: ~1K cache: 4 sinks + token_entropy_size 508 or 1020; decay_ratio 0.7-1.0.
task_sensitivity_findings: Streaming methods like StreamingLLM lose early-conversation facts, impairing long-term memory; SirLLM gives stable gains across tasks and models. Only method in this set with bespoke cross-turn recall workloads.

name: D2O
title: D2O: Dynamic Discriminative Operations for Efficient Long-Context Inference of Large Language Models (v1: '...Efficient Generative Inference...')
mechanism: Layer level: budget allocation driven by attention density. Token level: H2O-style eviction plus EMA-similarity re-discrimination that merges evicted tokens back into similar retained ones.
evaluated_benchmarks: Repo runners also for PIQA / OpenBookQA-5shot and HELM summarization (paper use likely)
budgets: Default 20% of prompt length (hh 0.1 + recent 0.1); scripts sweep 0.2/0.4/0.6/0.8.
task_sensitivity_findings: Largest gains on reasoning/multi-step generation (GSM8K, CoQA) for Llama-3-8B; on TruthfulQA it beats the full cache across Llama backbones and most budgets, which the authors read as pruning irrelevant context (single source).

name: CaM
title: CaM: Cache Merging for Memory-efficient LLMs Inference
mechanism: Merge to-be-evicted KV (values) into the retained cache via sampling driven by attention-score prominence, instead of discarding; layered on H2O/StreamingLLM eviction.
evaluated_benchmarks: lm-eval-harness QA/MC: OpenBookQA, MathQA, BoolQ, COPA, Winogrande (repo)
budgets: start_ratio/recent_ratio 0.1-0.2 of prompt; PPL runs 32 start + 32 recent tokens.
task_sensitivity_findings: Not recovered (unknown).

name: InfiniPot
title: InfiniPot: Infinite Context Processing on Memory-Constrained LLMs
mechanism: Continual Context Distillation: stream the input into a fixed KV 'pot' and compress on overflow, scoring tokens by Catalyst Prompt attention (a generic auxiliary prompt such as 'summarize the critical points') plus Novelty under Compression.
models: LLaMA-family and Mistral-family models (exact versions and meaning of 'M3' unknown)
budgets: Fixed 4K KV pot (also compared with 32K memory-unconstrained models).
task_sensitivity_findings: LongBench under 4K memory: M3-InfiniPot-4K 44.22 vs GPT-3.5-16K 43.74 and M3-PT-32K 47.84. Baselines: StreamingLLM 29.87, H2O 31.01, truncation 31.24, SirLLM 35.43, TOVA 36.26. Passkey holds to 1M with a 4K pot [likely: search summary].

name: Quest
title: Quest: Query-Aware Sparsity for Efficient Long-Context LLM Inference
mechanism: Non-evicting contrast: full KV kept in pages with per-page element-wise min/max keys; each decode step the query upper-bounds page criticality and attends only to the top-K pages (token budget).
evaluated_benchmarks: Passkey retrieval: 10K (LongChat-7B-v1.5-32K) and 100K (Yarn-Llama-2-7B-128K); later Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct 100K in repo
LongBench 6 tasks: Qasper, NarrativeQA, HotpotQA, MultiFieldQA-en, GovReport, TriviaQA
budgets: Token budget 64-4096 (passkey 64 at 10K, 1024 at 100K; LongBench 512/1024/2048/4096; PG-19 4096).
task_sensitivity_findings: Query-agnostic eviction (H2O, TOVA, StreamingLLM) discards the answer's KV before the question arrives and fails passkey (poster example: 2% vs 100%). Quest is near-perfect with ~1% of tokens. On LongBench, baselines need nearly the full cache to be lossless while Quest is lossless at ~2K. Summarization attends to different paragraphs sequentially, so criticality is query-dependent.

name: InfiniGen
title: InfiniGen: Efficient Generative Inference of Large Language Models with Dynamic KV Cache Management
mechanism: Offloading-based (FlexGen): KV in CPU memory; important tokens for the next layer are speculated from the current input with partial query weights and a skewed partial key cache, and only those are prefetched; CPU KV pool with FIFO/LRU/counter eviction.
evaluated_benchmarks: lm-eval-harness 5-shot: PIQA, OpenBookQA, WinoGrande, COPA, RTE
Block-wise perplexity per 256-token decoding chunk (WikiText-2) vs H2O
budgets: Fetch budget e.g. 0.2 with alpha thresholds 1-9 and partial-weight ratio 0.1-1.0; CPU pool capacity 100% or 80%; H2O baseline 1.875%+1.875% in the chunk-PPL test.
task_sensitivity_findings: H2O's perplexity drifts further from full cache as decoding continues (error accumulates over long generation); InfiniGen stays close to full cache.

name: ArkVale
title: ArkVale: Efficient Generative LLM Inference with Recallable Key-Value Eviction
mechanism: Page-based KV manager: filled pages are backed up to CPU and summarized as bounding-volume digests of their keys (cuboid-mean); each step pages are scored against the query, important evicted pages are recalled, and only the top pages are attended.
evaluated_benchmarks: LongBench 6: HotpotQA, NarrativeQA, Qasper, GovReport, TriviaQA, PassageRetrieval
Passkey retrieval at 10K/20K/30K (20 cases each, depths 0-95%)
budgets: Cache budget 512/1024/2048/4096 tokens; page size 16 or 32; first two layers uncompressed.
task_sensitivity_findings: Token importance drifts (a GovReport page becomes critical ~4,500 tokens later). With question-after-context (two-phase prefill), permanent-eviction baselines score 0-40% on passkey, lower at longer context or smaller budget; ArkVale stays >=95%. On LongBench, baselines lag noticeably below 2048 and even at 4096. ArkVale matches full at 512 for TriviaQA, 1024 for HotpotQA/Qasper, 2048 for NarrativeQA/PassageRetrieval.

name: LESS
title: Get More with LESS: Synthesizing Recurrence with KV Cache Compression for Efficient LLM Inference
mechanism: An eviction policy (H2O or sinks+recent) augmented with a small, constant-size learned low-rank recurrent state that absorbs the residual of evicted tokens so all tokens stay queryable; cheap per-layer training.
budgets: E.g. H2O at 5% (2.5% heavy + 2.5% recent) with a 'Baseline+' control given matched extra memory; 10% H2O for Falcon.
task_sensitivity_findings: Eviction policies 'have limited success in tasks that require recollecting a majority of previous tokens'; LESS narrows the gap to full cache, sometimes matching it.

name: VATP
title: Attention Score is not All You Need for Token Importance Indicator in KV Cache Reduction: Value Also Matters
mechanism: Value-Aware Token Pruning: importance = accumulated attention score x L1 norm of the value vector; plugged into H2O or Scissorhands with protected attention-sink tokens (20).
evaluated_benchmarks: LongBench (16 English datasets: NarrativeQA, Qasper, MultiFieldQA-en, HotpotQA, 2WikiMQA, MuSiQue, GovReport, QMSum, MultiNews, TREC, TriviaQA, SAMSum, PassageCount, PassageRetrieval-en, LCC, RepoBench-P)
budgets: 50% KV budget (heavy_ratio 0.25 + recent); simulated by masking, not real eviction.
task_sensitivity_findings: Beats attention-only baselines (H2O, Scissorhands) on more than 12 of 16 LongBench tasks; which tasks it loses on is unknown.

name: LM-Infinite
title: LM-Infinite: Zero-Shot Extreme Length Generalization for Large Language Models
mechanism: Lambda-shaped attention mask (first n_starting tokens + most recent L_pretrain tokens) plus a relative-distance ceiling; functionally the same retained set as StreamingLLM.
evaluated_benchmarks: Perplexity on ArXiv and OpenWebText2 (Pile subsets), up to 200M tokens
Generation quality (BLEU/ROUGE) on ArXiv at positions 4K-16K
budgets: Local branch = pretraining length (2K/4K); global (starting) branch 10-100 tokens.
task_sensitivity_findings: Keeps perplexity stable to 200M tokens with 2.7x decoding speedup and 7.5x memory saving. For passkey, the repo script enables top-k attention to middle tokens from layer 4, implying the pure Lambda-mask cannot retrieve content outside its window [likely].

name: RoCo (EasyKV)
title: On the Efficacy of Eviction Policy for Key-Value Constrained Generative Language Model Inference
mechanism: Robust Cache Omission: score tokens by temporal (averaged) attention plus a robustness term (attention standard deviation); a systematic study of importance-score and eviction-scope choices (persistence-of-importance follow-up).
evaluated_benchmarks: Repo examples: passkey retrieval (Vicuna-7B-16K at 10K; NTK-scaled LLaMa2-7B-Chat at 5K), news summarization, instruction following (LLaMa2-7B-Chat), perplexity (LLaMa2-13B)
Paper (secondary summary): language modeling, summarization, context reconstruction, AlpacaEval [likely]
budgets: Prefill budget as a fraction (e.g. 0.5); decode budget in tokens (e.g. 150-300); RoCo reportedly matches full cache at 40% on AlpacaEval [likely].
task_sensitivity_findings: Gains are larger on generative tasks than on language modeling because errors accumulate [likely: secondary summary].

name: Ada-KV
title: Ada-KV: Optimizing KV Cache Eviction by Adaptive Budget Allocation for Efficient LLM Inference
mechanism: Reallocate each layer's KV budget across heads by attention concentration; plugs into SnapKV/PyramidKV; flattened variable-length per-head cache with flash_attn_varlen.
budgets: base_capacity e.g. 512 per head-average (README example); paper sweeps unknown.
task_sensitivity_findings: README: adaptive head budgets give substantial gains on RULER sub-tasks when added to SnapKV/PyramidKV; per-task statements unknown.

name: SqueezeAttention
title: SqueezeAttention: 2D Management of KV-Cache in LLM Inference via Layer-wise Optimal Budget
mechanism: Cluster layers by importance (cosine similarity of hidden states before/after attention), reallocate per-layer KV budgets, then apply a token policy (sliding window, StreamingLLM or H2O) per layer.
evaluated_benchmarks: 'A wide range of LLMs and benchmarks' (full list unknown)
budgets: E.g. 21% of prompt per layer (SAMSum), 40% (XSUM); layer-class budgets reallocated (e.g. 0.21 -> 0.08 for less important layers).
task_sensitivity_findings: 30-70% memory reduction and up to 2.2x throughput; per-task statements unknown.

name: InfLLM
title: InfLLM: Unveiling the Intrinsic Capacity of LLMs for Understanding Extremely Long Sequences with Training-Free Memory
mechanism: Non-evicting contrast: sinks + local window, with distant context stored in block memory units (optionally CPU-offloaded) and retrieved per step via representative tokens / top-k (optional faiss).
budgets: Configured via YAML (local window, memory block size, top-k blocks); specific values not recovered.
task_sensitivity_findings: Not recovered (unknown).
